thread:
marta: heads up — getting multiple customer reports of intermittent 502s from hosted inference this morning. looks correlated to cache hits on prefix-kv. sample customer request-id: r-0a1b2c3d. see gateway error in logs below.

kevin: on it. can you paste the exact log lines and a repro curl? also which model and region?

marta: model: gpt-lite-compat v2, region: us-west-2. repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
Gateway error we see:
```
2026-03-17T10:12:33.442Z ERROR gateway proxy: upstream request failed: status=502 reason="upstream memcached timeout" svc=hosted-inference route=/v1/generate request_id=r-0a1b2c3d cache_op="prefix_kv.get" shard="shard-3" duration_ms=2510
```

ashley_sre: i’m seeing memcached shard-3 p99 latencies spike right at 10:10–10:20. metrics: p50=12ms p95=430ms p99=1.3s, conn_drops=42 in last 10m. 5xx rate for hosted-api jumped from 0.8% -> 6.2% in same window. looks like a hot shard / eviction storm. :thinking_face:

sre_oncall_bot: ALERT memcached-shard-3 latency > 1s (10:11) — rule memcached.latency.p99 — severity=high — affected: hosted-inference (rate 5xx +4.4%)

marta: customer impact: some requests are failing on first token and retrying causes double charge complaints. they shared timestamps and example ids. they asked for ETA and a possible mitigation ASAP.

kevin: immediate mitigation options: 1) enable cache-bypass for affected customer (route header X-Cache-Bypass: true) 2) flip policy to fallback to redis for prefix cache for that tenant 3) scale memcached pool / restart shard-3 node (risky). i'd push (1) + (2) short-term. who can run the bypass?

infra-bot: runbook: to set tenant-level bypass: `POST /internal/tenants/<tenant>/config {"prefix_kv.bypass": true}` — requires infra-admin role. to set runtime fallback: set env `PREFIX_CACHE_FALLBACK=redis` on pool config, then rollout canary.

marta: i tested setting X-Cache-Bypass locally and the request succeeds (200) with latency ~120ms. customer agreed to temporary bypass.

support_lead: please open an ENG ticket and @eng-runtime. include logs, metrics snapshot, and tenant id. tell customer: temporary bypass enabled, engineering investigating shard health, ETA for deeper update in 90m. :thumbsup:

kevin: opened ENG-5421 and pinged eng-runtime. included logs + Grafana snapshots + repro curl. assigned to @alex-runtime.

ashley_sre: plan for next 60m: 1) keep bypass on for impacted tenants 2) run memcached shard diagnostics (scrub backlog, check network IO, mem pressure) 3) if shard remains hot, re-shard the prefix mapping or roll the node. i'll start diagnostics now.

marta: customer notified with temporary workaround and ETA. they confirmed reduced 502s after bypass. sending them a follow-up note. :relieved:

kevin: update — alex-runtime says initial heap fragmentation + prefetch loop for a specific prefix caused repeated thundering. engineering will push a fix to limit prefetch concurrency for that prefix and to auto-route heavy prefixes to fallback cache. tentative rollout in 3h canary, full rollout next-day if clean.

support_lead: good. owners: ashley_sre (incident lead), kevin (support lead), alex-runtime (eng owner). postmortem owner: kevin. set severity P2 and track billing impact separately.

infra-bot: escalation ticket SYS-1898 created to track memcached node replacement and re-sharding actions.

marta: closing the support thread after customer confirms improved behavior. will reopen if regressions. :white_check_mark:
